subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: On normal gateway SIGTERM/SIGINT, should OpenClaw cancel managed active/background exec child processes before the shutdown watchdog, preserve yielded/background work, or defer that behavior to a separate session/process-control surface?
rationale: Current tests intentionally preserve active runs on normal shutdown, while resolving this report likely requires changing that lifecycle contract or adding a bounded exception for managed child processes.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: Normal stop would reject new work, drain briefly, then cancel managed exec/process scopes before the watchdog while documenting explicit preservation exceptions.

options.title: Preserve background work on normal stop
options.body: OpenClaw would keep current normal-stop behavior and improve diagnostics for the child process responsible for shutdown timeouts.

options.title: Defer to session kill design
options.body: This issue would wait for the broader session/process list-and-kill contract tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: Normal stop would reject new work, drain briefly, then cancel managed exec/process scopes before the watchdog while documenting explicit preservation exceptions.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a core lifecycle/product contract choice, and recent gateway lifecycle history makes this the strongest routing candidate.
